brand.title: Passport
brand.homeHint: Choose a language and open the passport.
brand.catalogHint: Select one wonder and place its stamp.
brand.detailHint: Read, answer one question, and validate the stamp.

home.title: Start your passport of the 14 wonders
home.subtitle: Move from the seven ancient wonders to the seven new wonders. Each stop unlocks one stamp in your travel passport.
home.welcomeCopy: Explore the wonders, answer the questions, and unlock your stamps.

catalog.title: All fourteen wonders
catalog.subtitle: Open any card to see the passport page, read the short context, and answer one question.
catalog.summaryText: Each wonder has one dedicated stamp and one passport slot. A correct answer fills the slot and advances your route.

detail.slotEmpty: Answer the question to place this stamp.
detail.questionHint: Choose the right answer to validate the stamp.
detail.correct: Correct answer. The stamp is now placed in the passport.
detail.incorrect: Not yet. Select another answer to place the stamp.

great-pyramid.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
great-pyramid.summary: The oldest and only surviving ancient wonder rises on the Giza plateau as a royal tomb built with precise stone engineering.
great-pyramid.passportNote: This is the only ancient wonder that still stands today.

question.prompt: In which country can you visit the Great Pyramid of Giza?

hanging-gardens.name: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
hanging-gardens.summary: Legend describes terraced gardens watered above the desert skyline of ancient Babylon.
hanging-gardens.passportNote: No confirmed ruins have been found, which makes this page part history and part mystery.

question.prompt: Ancient Babylon is usually associated with which present-day country?

statue-zeus.name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
statue-zeus.summary: A monumental seated statue once dominated Olympia and celebrated Zeus at the heart of the games.
statue-zeus.passportNote: This passport page remembers a wonder known mostly through written accounts and coins.

question.prompt: Olympia, the site of this wonder, is in which country?

temple-artemis.name: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
temple-artemis.summary: A vast marble sanctuary at Ephesus honored Artemis and drew pilgrims from around the Mediterranean.
temple-artemis.passportNote: The temple was rebuilt more than once, turning memory and ruin into one story.

question.prompt: Ephesus is located in which modern country?

mausoleum-halicarnassus.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
mausoleum-halicarnassus.summary: This ornate royal tomb gave the world the word mausoleum through its scale, sculpture, and ceremony.
mausoleum-halicarnassus.passportNote: Its memory survives in architecture every time we describe a monumental tomb.

question.prompt: Halicarnassus stood on the coast of which present-day country?

colossus-rhodes.name: Colossus of Rhodes
colossus-rhodes.summary: A giant bronze figure welcomed sailors near the harbor of Rhodes after a hard-fought victory.
colossus-rhodes.passportNote: The statue stood only a few decades, but its image became permanent in world memory.

question.prompt: Rhodes belongs to which country today?

lighthouse-alexandria.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
lighthouse-alexandria.summary: The Pharos of Alexandria guided ships with fire and mirrored light at one of the busiest ports of the ancient world.
lighthouse-alexandria.passportNote: This stamp honors a wonder that turned navigation into spectacle.

question.prompt: Alexandria is in which country today?

great-wall.name: Great Wall of China
great-wall.summary: A chain of fortifications crosses mountains and deserts, showing how defense and landscape were linked over centuries.
great-wall.passportNote: It is not one single wall, but a long system built and rebuilt through time.

question.prompt: The Great Wall is in which country?

petra.name: Petra
petra.summary: Petra is a rock-carved city whose facades open from narrow desert canyons into monumental spaces.
petra.passportNote: Its stamp belongs to a city shaped as much by trade routes as by stone.

question.prompt: Petra is located in which country?

colosseum.name: Colosseum
colosseum.summary: Rome's great amphitheater staged spectacle, engineering skill, and imperial power in one enduring oval.
colosseum.passportNote: The passport slot marks a monument built for crowds, ritual, and performance.

question.prompt: In which country is the Colosseum?

chichen-itza.name: Chichen Itza
chichen-itza.summary: This Maya city combines astronomy, ceremony, and stone geometry around the pyramid of El Castillo.
chichen-itza.passportNote: Its page connects architecture with calendars, shadow, and ritual movement.

question.prompt: Chichen Itza is in which country?

machu-picchu.name: Machu Picchu
machu-picchu.summary: High in the Andes, Machu Picchu aligns terraces, water, and sacred topography in a dramatic mountain setting.
machu-picchu.passportNote: This stamp celebrates a site where engineering follows the terrain instead of erasing it.

question.prompt: Machu Picchu is in which country?

taj-mahal.name: Taj Mahal
taj-mahal.summary: A marble mausoleum of symmetry and light, the Taj Mahal transforms grief into a carefully staged landscape.
taj-mahal.passportNote: Its passport page is about memory, devotion, and crafted balance.

question.prompt: The Taj Mahal is in which country?

christ-redeemer.name: Christ the Redeemer
christ-redeemer.summary: The hilltop statue above Rio de Janeiro has become a global image of welcome and horizon.
christ-redeemer.passportNote: This stamp represents a modern wonder shaped by both sculpture and skyline.

question.prompt: Christ the Redeemer overlooks which country?
